title: Naive cotangent complex on the small etale site of an algebraic space
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Work with sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, whose objects are etale scheme charts and whose coverings are jointly surjective etale families. Use its existing equivalent small affine ringed model [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], with the actual regular-functions sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ in the original section universe, and use the same module category and $D(\mathcal O_X)$ as [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus], with arbitrary localization morphism universe. Transport the canonical ring inverse image and its structure map through the affine-basis restriction equivalences; do not enlarge the universe of module sections. Use the canonical morphism of ringed topoi for $f$ supplied by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ be its inverse-image functor, put $\mathcal A=f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$ and $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_X$, and use the structure map $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. Form $\mathcal P=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal A(U)[\mathcal B(U)]$, the polynomial algebra [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with one variable $[b]$ for every section $b\in\mathcal B(U)$. For a chart map $V\to U$, restriction sends coefficients by $\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal A(V)$ and sends $[b]$ to $[b|_V]$. Let $\mathcal I$ be the ideal subsheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-ideal] given by the kernel of evaluation $\mathcal P\to\mathcal B$, $[b]\mapsto b$. Evaluation is surjective as a sheaf map: every section $b$ is the image of the section represented by the variable $[b]$. Let $\mathcal I^2$ be the ideal subsheaf whose sections locally are finite sums of products of two sections of $\mathcal I$, and let $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be the sheaf quotient. Its $\mathcal B$-module structure is the one induced by evaluation $\mathcal P/\mathcal I\cong\mathcal B$. Explicitly, for a local section $b$ of $\mathcal B$ choose a lift $p$ in $\mathcal P$ and set $b\cdot\overline g=\overline{pg}$; changing $p$ to another lift $p'$ changes $pg$ by $(p-p')g\in\mathcal I^2$, and changing $g$ by a section of $\mathcal I^2$ also leaves this class unchanged because $\mathcal I^2$ is an ideal subsheaf. Define $\Omega_{\mathcal P/\mathcal A}$ by sheafifying [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the sectionwise modules of Kahler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], with restriction $p\,\mathrm dq\mapsto p|_V\,\mathrm d(q|_V)$. The naive cotangent complex is
$$\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}=\bigl[\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\xrightarrow{\,g\mapsto\mathrm dg\otimes1\,}\Omega_{\mathcal P/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P}\mathcal B\bigr],$$
in degrees $-1,0$, with zero terms in all other degrees and zero other differentials. Tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and quotients are taken in module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The displayed differential sends the class of a local section $g$ of $\mathcal I$ to $\mathrm dg\otimes1$; it is well-defined since $\mathrm d(gh)\otimes1=\mathrm dg\otimes h+\mathrm dh\otimes g=0$ for $g,h\in\mathcal I$, and is $\mathcal B$-linear: for $p\in\mathcal P$ and $g\in\mathcal I$, $\mathrm d(pg)\otimes1=p\,\mathrm dg\otimes1+\mathrm dp\otimes g=p\,\mathrm dg\otimes1$, with the $p$-action factoring through $\mathcal P/\mathcal I=\mathcal B$. These formulas commute with restrictions because restriction preserves multiplication and the displayed rule for differentials. We use the same notation for its image in $D(\mathcal O_X)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For any $E,F\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, write $\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal O_X}(E,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,F[n])$; a sheaf used as $F$ is placed in degree zero.

split_report.summary: Audited the definition against Stacks 0D0V, 08TW and 08U0. Reused the existing canonical algebraic-space ringed-topos map, ringed-topos morphism, polynomial-ring, sheafification, ideal-subsheaf and module-sheafification nodes. Made restrictions, evaluation lifts, the ideal square, quotient module structure and differential explicit. The quotient action is independent of the lift because two lifts differ by an element of the kernel and their products with a kernel section differ by an element of the square; the Leibniz calculation checks the differential directly. The item states this for A = f^{-1}O_Y -> O_X on X_et, in D(Mod O_X), with no added hypotheses. This is the fourth head; 7db0c6ff, 764bb227 and b8075577 passed. A DAG search finds no duplicate definition. statement_change.what: The existing equivalent small ringed model and its derived-module calculus were not cited, leaving the presentation of O_X, Mod(O_X) and D(O_X) unspecified. The returned implementation used module sections in u+1, which includes strictly more sheaves than the existing section-universe-u category. Explicitly use the existing affine-basis model and its original section universe, and transport the canonical ring inverse image through its restriction equivalence. This fixes the presentation of Stacks 0D0V without changing its mathematics.

citers.note: The affine polynomial presentation and its derived comparison use the same rings, conormal and differentials under affine-basis restriction.
Square-zero extensions and derived Ext are transported by the same ringed-site equivalence, including arbitrary module coefficients and degrees zero and one.
The deformation Ext groups retain the original module coefficients and canonical structural map under the restriction equivalence.
The canonical comparison still uses the same regular-functions ring map and polynomial complex, now represented in the existing small-model derived category.
Coherence, boundedness and degree-zero structure sheaves are preserved by the specified restriction equivalence in the original module universe.
The canonical inverse image and ring map are transported through the basis equivalences, so etale localization has the same meaning.
Affine-chart restriction, quasi-coherence and local finite presentations are unchanged by the specified small-model equivalence.
The cohomology is tested by the existing module equivalence, exactly as in the cited derived-module calculus; vanishing degrees are unchanged.
The Hom tests and extension classification are in the existing original-universe derived category, with the same unrestricted coefficient modules.
